text:
leah: Quick heads-up — running a targeted preemptible eviction game day in us-west-2 tomorrow 10:30 PT. Goal: validate mixed-capacity pool failover and graceful degradation.

sanjay: +1. What's the scope? All model-serving pools or a subset?

leah: subset: gpu-pool-general (70% spot, 30% reserved) and gpu-pool-lowpri (100% preemptible). We'll simulate 30% concurrent evictions across AZs.

mike: Can we make sure control plane (dedicated schedulers) aren't affected? We only want worker node evictions.

leah: yes — eviction script only triggers cloud provider preemption API on node groups. Control plane untouched.

olivia: Reminder: add feature flags for canary routing so we can divert traffic to reserved-only pools if things degrade. I put a stub in the runbook: `/scripts/route-canary --to reserved`

deploy-bot: [scheduled] preempt-eviction-run starts 2025-05-21T17:30:00Z. Run ID: run-20250521-evict1

jordan: Success criteria proposal:
• No customer-facing 5xxs from inference endpoints attributable to capacity loss.
• Sustained throughput drop <15% for >10 minutes.
• Tail latency (p99) increase capped at 2x baseline for under 5 minutes.
• Autoscaler recovers node deficit within target window (AZ-local: 3m, cross-AZ failover: 8m).

cassie: Add: cache hit ratio for KV-cache should remain >= 85% (we want to validate cold-start behavior too).

sanjay: Ops checklist I pushed to the runbook:
```
- Pre-check: snapshot running model replicas per pool
- Verify reserved pool watermark >= 20% free capacity
- Disable low-priority rollout jobs
- Increase logging level for scheduler and autoscaler
- Alerting: temp alert on scaledown > expected
```

leah: Eviction script will use exponential ramp: 5% at T0, +5% each minute until 30% or we abort. Abort conditions: any 5xx spike >0.5% or control-plane errors.

mike: For interruption handling tests, run an additional case where KV cache misses spike — we should observe batching backpressure. Need trace IDs preserved to correlate.

olivia: I'll wire the trace tag in the canary header: `X-GameDay-Run: run-20250521-evict1` and add automatic eval harness to run a 10k sample of synthetic requests during the window.

jordan: On rollback: we keep a fast path to route all traffic to dedicated pools (`/ops/route --to dedicated --force`) and a slower path to spin up extra dedicated instances if needed. Documented in the runbook with playbook link.

cassie: Metrics to capture:
- per-pool allocated GPUs
- replicas per model
- queue length per worker
- per-request latency histograms
- cache hit rate
- cost burn (estimated) during event

sanjay: Cost note: anticipate a short-term on-demand spike. Budget owner = @mike, expected delta ~ +$X for the window (I opened a ticket to estimate).

leah: Postmortem template: short timeline, incident map (evicted nodes -> rescheduled pods -> routing changes), divergences from runbook, lessons. Aim to close within 3 business days.

deploy-bot: [run] eviction phase 1 (5%) started at 17:30:00Z. Nodes evicted: 12.

mike: seeing increased queue length on gpu-pool-general, but no 5xxs yet. autoscaler scale-up pending 60s cooldown.

olivia: synthetic load running now, trace header in place.

cassie: KV cache hit dip to 72% for 90s, then warmed back up to 88% after reroutes.

jordan: p99 latency bumped 1.6x for ~2:10. within tolerance. throughput -12% sustained for 7m.

sanjay: Abort? Any 5xxs?

mike: No 5xx spike. Control plane stable. Recommend continue to 30%. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: [run] eviction phase final (30%) completed at 17:37:20Z. Nodes evicted total: 72.

leah: Nice — initial takeaway: mixed pools + canary routing maintained availability. Need follow-ups: 1) tighten autoscaler responsiveness, 2) pre-warm KV caches on reserved pool, 3) add off-ramp when latency exceeds 2x for >3m.

cassie: I will draft cache pre-warm job: `cron: prewarm-kv --pool reserved --concurrency 20` and test it in staging.

olivia: I'll produce the synthetic load eval report and attach traces. Expect a 1-2 page summary by EOD.

jordan: I'll update success criteria thresholds to be slightly stricter based on these numbers and add them to the SLO docs.

leah: Great work team — no customer impact and the runbook behaved as expected. Postmortem checklist: assign owner, attach logs, runbook edits. I'll open the postmortem draft.

sanjay: Thanks everyone. Suggest next drill: cross-region preempt (us-west-2 -> failover eu-west-1) in 2 weeks to exercise routing across regions.

mike: +1. We'll schedule and add network egress checks for cold-cache cross-region latency.

leah: Filing follow-up tasks now. Closing thread after postmortem draft is posted. :white_check_mark:
